title: The Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002 & 2023 Amendments
source_citation: Ministry of Cooperation, Gazette of India, Act No. 39 of 2002 & Act No. 11 of 2023
content: The Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002 governs cooperative societies whose objects are not confined to one State and serve the interests of members in more than one State. Under Section 25, any multi-state cooperative society may admit individuals, other cooperative societies, and government entities as members. Section 41 establishes the democratic control of multi-state cooperatives, requiring that every member shall have one vote regardless of the number of shares held. Section 45 mandates regular board elections conducted by the Co-operative Election Authority established under the 2023 Amendment. Section 84 provides for the reference of disputes touching the constitution, management or business of a multi-state cooperative society to arbitration by the Central Registrar or an arbitrator appointed by the Registrar. The 2023 amendment established the Co-operative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund for reviving sick multi-state cooperatives and introduced Co-operative Information Officers to facilitate transparency.

title: Model Bye-Laws for Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS)
source_citation: Ministry of Cooperation, Model Bye-Laws for PACS, 2022-2023
content: Model Bye-laws enable Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) to diversify their business activities beyond short-term crop loans into over 25 diversified commercial sectors. Under the Model Bye-Laws, PACS can establish and operate Custom Hiring Centres (CHC) for farm machinery, community irrigation projects, warehouse storage facilities, Kisan Seva Kendras for fertilizer and pesticide distribution, LPG distribution agencies, fair price shops (PDS), and decentralized grain storage under the World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector. Membership in PACS is open to all farmers, agricultural labourers, and rural artisans residing within the society's area of operation. All active members who transact minimum business with the society have the democratic right to vote in the General Body meeting and contest Managing Committee elections. The Secretary/CEO is appointed by the Board of Directors to manage daily administrative affairs and ensure transparent computerized accounts.

title: Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of 63,000 PACS
source_citation: Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), June 2022 / Ministry of Cooperation
content: The Project for Computerization of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) has a total budgetary outlay of Rs 2,516 Crore approved by the Government of India. The objective is to onboard 63,000 functional PACS onto an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) based Common National Software. The system integrates PACS directly with District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), linking them upstream to NABARD. Key benefits include financial transparency, real-time auditing, automation of credit disbursement, electronic maintenance of land and crop records, cyber security safeguards, and direct delivery of DBT subsidies to farmers' bank accounts. Each participating PACS receives hardware procurement assistance including biometric devices, desktop computers, printers, and uninterrupted power supply (UPS), backed by cloud data hosting on MeghRaj.

title: NCDC Yuva Sahakar — Cooperative Enterprise Support Scheme
source_citation: National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) Operational Guidelines
content: Yuva Sahakar is a flagship youth-focused cooperative scheme launched by the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) to encourage young entrepreneurs to form and expand cooperative startups in agribusiness, processing, cold chains, logistics, and renewable energy. Cooperatives that have been in operation for at least one year and have at least 100 members, with at least 50% youth members (aged between 18 and 35 years), or newly formed cooperatives exclusively by youth, are eligible. The scheme provides term loans of up to 80% of the project cost for projects up to Rs 3 Crore for general cooperatives, and up to 85% for cooperatives with 100% SC/ST/Women/PWD members or located in the North Eastern Region. An interest incentive of 2% per annum is granted on prompt repayment. Financial assistance covers capital investment in infrastructure, machinery, and working capital.

title: NCDC Ayushman Sahakar — Healthcare Infrastructure for Cooperatives
source_citation: National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) Health Guidelines
content: Ayushman Sahakar is a dedicated financial assistance scheme formulated by NCDC to assist cooperative societies in creating healthcare, medical education, diagnostic, and wellness infrastructure in rural and semi-urban areas. Any cooperative society with suitable healthcare or hospital development provisions in its registered bye-laws is eligible for loans. The scheme funds the establishment, modernizing, and expansion of hospitals, medical and nursing colleges, diagnostic testing laboratories, wellness centres, Ayurvedic and Yoga centres, tele-medicine facilities, and ambulance services. Working capital and margin money assistance are also covered. Cooperatives with majority women members receive a 1% interest rate concession. Projects can access term loans with repayment tenures of up to 8 years including moratorium periods.

title: Dairy Sahakar Scheme for Milk Cooperatives
source_citation: Ministry of Cooperation & National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC)
content: The Dairy Sahakar scheme with an outlay of Rs 5,000 Crore implemented through NCDC extends financial support to eligible cooperative societies operating in the dairy and cattle feed sector. Beneficiaries include primary dairy cooperatives, district milk unions, and state dairy federations. Financial assistance provides funding for establishing modern chilling centers, milk processing plants, automated milk collection units, cattle feed factories, cold chain transport logistics, laboratory quality testing equipment, and export infrastructure. It strengthens farm-gate dairy value addition, improves income for smallholder milk producers, and ensures timely milk payments directly into farmer bank accounts.
